payload.body:
**0081 + 0084: your F1 to F4 are folded at 6608146, on top of your 0083 fold at 63ee125, for your re-verify.** Four paths: RELEASES/0.1.2.md (the 0081 and 0084 entries only), CHANGELOG.md (regenerated), tests/unit/helpers.bats and tests/unit/review.bats. Gates at commit: guards 4 ran, critic (shell) enforced, doctor estate clean. Not pushed.

**F1, the 0081 sentence.** dc measured it too, at d6cb655 through the dispatcher: a throwaway probe in an export, `languages: [shell]`, referent declared. root_var DEVBIN_RUN_ID, DEVBIN_RUN_STAMP, DEVBIN_RUN_REFERENT and DEVBIN_CLI_TASK held the project root at rc 0. DEVBIN_LANGUAGES held `shell` and DEVBIN_FMT_ARMS was empty, so the root was lost. An option (flag, value OPTVAL) exporting into any of the six put OPTVAL there at rc 0. The control NONE_OF_DEVBINS got the root and OPTVAL at both commits, and at 437ee26 all twelve runs exit 1 naming the value. The entry now reads "... and so did `DEVBIN_RUN_STAMP`, `DEVBIN_RUN_REFERENT` and `DEVBIN_CLI_TASK`; a `root_var` naming `DEVBIN_LANGUAGES` or `DEVBIN_FMT_ARMS` got devbin's value in place of the project root, and an option exporting into any of the six put its own value there." Its test claim is scoped to F4's four paths: "every name devbin adds to the environment of a project handler, an option's `run:`, alone and under `all`, and a `notes.run` command".

**F2, the bound.** helpers.bats 63, after the misread-loop arm. l0 names the file and each l<k> names l<k-1>, grown until the first l<n> leads to no file (n=32 here); then replace_file through l<n-1>. It fails if the chain grew past 100 (no limit found) or stopped below 8 (nothing measured), and asserts success, the file replaced, and the link still naming l<n-2>. Your R5 (bound 1) reddens 59 and 63; R5b (2) and R5c (31) redden 63 alone, at assert_success, reading "cannot tell which file .../l31 is a symbolic link to". At d6cb655's helpers it is red at "the file at the end of a chain of 32 links was not replaced: old". On the Ubuntu runner it walks Linux's own limit.

**F3, the limits.** dc measured both through the functions, at d6cb655 and 437ee26 alike. My fixture was one directory short at first, and its dangle check caught it. copy_vendored over a vendored file that is a link: rc 0, the link now a regular file holding the new bytes, the file it named still old. Every call sits behind `install` or `upgrade`: publish_install (lib/install:237, called from lib/cmd/install:320 and lib/cmd/upgrade:123), lib/cmd/install:328, and lib/cmd/upgrade:280 and 318. The entry: "**Two limits:** a hard link is still split by the rename, as it always was, and `install` and `upgrade` still replace a vendored file that is a link with a regular file, leaving the file it named as it was." Your refusal, re-measured: a write through a link into a read-only directory had rc 0 and replaced the link at d6cb655; at 437ee26 it has rc 1, the link and target intact, no temporary, and says "could not create a temporary file beside .../rw/../ro/t". The entry: "Writing through a link to a file in a directory that cannot be written is refused, naming that file, where it replaced the link with a regular file at exit 0."

**F4, the fourth source.** review.bats 8. The fixture enables release with notes.kind command and notes.run `bin/notes-env`, a stub that appends `env` to env.notes and answers views-check `none` and state `open`, beside VERSION 1.0.0. The arm runs `release check` scrubbed, asserts success and that env.notes exists, and reads it with the other three sources. The comment names four paths. Your R6 (`DEVBIN_PROBE_NOTES=1` in _notes_command_env's export) reddens 8 alone, at "may still take: DEVBIN_PROBE_NOTES".

**Runs.** At the landing tree, 63ee125 plus these four paths (52bcca0 and 32c7a8a touch none of them): helpers.bats 1..64, 64 ok; review.bats 1..25, 25 ok; `release notes`, then `release check` 2 of 2 views current, rc 0. Each landed blob cmp-equals the tested file, and the note's diff is the 0081 and 0084 lines alone. No full suite: no file under lib/ changed, and both arms' files ran whole. Every mutant restore was cmp-equal, with lib/ clean after.

**Lesson candidate (your call):** F1's wrong clause was written from the list of six names, not from driving each one, and two of the six went the other way. A claim about each member of a list wants a run per member.
